title: AEOeye vs AthenaHQ: Free Instant Audit vs Paid GEO Platform
metaDescription: AEOeye vs AthenaHQ compared: free instant AI visibility audit vs a $295/mo GEO platform. Pricing, engines, speed, and who each tool is genuinely best for.
shortAnswer: AEOeye and AthenaHQ solve the same problem at different stages. AEOeye gives you a free, instant audit of whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini recommend your brand — no contract, no sales call. AthenaHQ is a paid GEO platform ($295/mo, no free trial) built for teams that need ongoing monitoring, citation analytics, and ROI reporting. Start with AEOeye to see where you stand; consider AthenaHQ when you're ready to commit to continuous tracking.
intro:
If you're weighing **AEOeye vs AthenaHQ**, you're really choosing between two different moments in the same journey. One answers "Do AI engines recommend my brand right now?" in a few minutes, for free. The other is a budgeted platform for teams running a continuous AI-search program.

This is a fair, factual head-to-head. We'll be honest about where AthenaHQ is genuinely stronger — and where AEOeye's free, instant, multi-engine approach makes more sense — so you can pick the right tool for your situation rather than the one with the louder pitch.

sections.heading: The core difference: see first, vs. commit first
sections.body:
The cleanest way to separate these tools is *when you pay*.

With **AEOeye**, you run the audit before spending anything. You enter your brand and the buyer questions that matter, and it blind-queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini to show whether you're recommended, where you rank, and which competitors win the answer. No card, no contract, no demo call. You see your AI visibility, then decide what to do.

**AthenaHQ** flips that order. There's no free tier and no true free trial, so you commit to the Self-Serve plan at $295/month (softened by a discounted ~$95 first month that still requires upfront payment) before you see your own results. In exchange you get an ongoing platform — dashboards, sentiment and mention analytics, competitor benchmarking, and citation tracking that runs continuously.

Neither order is wrong. If you want a quick, honest read on where you stand, see-first wins. If you already know you need a managed program and have budget allocated, commit-first gets you straight into the tooling.

sections.heading: Pricing, credits, and what's actually included
sections.body:
AEOeye is free to start and instant, so the entry cost is your time. Its deepest multi-engine querying activates with usage rather than a tier you pre-pay for.

AthenaHQ's pricing is the most common concern reviewers raise — not because it's unreasonable for the market, but because it's hard to forecast. The Self-Serve plan is $295/month with 3,600 credits, where roughly one credit equals one tracked AI response. Monitoring many prompts across multiple engines or regions burns credits fast, and teams report running out mid-month and buying overages (about $0.08/credit, or $100 per 1,250). So the real monthly bill can exceed the sticker price.

There's also a feature-tier consideration. Several capabilities that shine in demos are Enterprise-only (custom pricing, commonly $2,000+/mo): the ACE citation engine, multi-region and persona targeting, API and BI integrations, and SSO. Self-Serve is limited to a single country and basic tooling, so multi-market teams sometimes find they need an Enterprise contract sooner than expected. Budget for the plan you'll actually need, not just the one you start on.

sections.heading: AI engines and depth of analysis
sections.body:
Both tools query across the major AI engines. **AEOeye** runs blind, multi-engine queries against ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini, focused on the practical question buyers care about: are you recommended, and who beats you?

This is where it's fair to give **AthenaHQ** real credit. As a dedicated platform, it goes deeper on *ongoing* analytics — mention and sentiment trends over time, structured competitor benchmarking, and citation tracking that shows which sources and content types AI engines pull from. Its action center turns those findings into specific content fixes, and it integrates with Shopify and GA4 to help e-commerce teams tie AI visibility to revenue. For a team that needs to *prove* AI-search ROI to stakeholders month over month, that historical, dashboard-driven depth is a genuine advantage AEOeye doesn't fully match yet.

The honest framing: AEOeye is stronger for an instant, no-commitment snapshot and competitor read; AthenaHQ is stronger for sustained, enterprise-grade measurement and reporting once you've committed the budget and time.

sections.heading: Setup, speed, and learning curve
sections.body:
**AEOeye** is built so a non-expert gets value in one sitting. There's no onboarding, no credit budgeting, and nothing to configure beyond your brand and the questions you want tested. First results arrive in minutes, and the output is plain-language: recommended or not, your rank, the competitors winning the answer.

**AthenaHQ** is a platform, and platforms have a learning curve — which is appropriate for what it does. You'll connect data sources (e.g., Shopify/GA4), set up the prompts and competitors you want to track, and learn how credits map to your monitoring scope so you don't exhaust them early. That investment pays off for a team running a continuous program, but it's more than a curious solopreneur or a small team wants to take on just to answer "how visible am I in AI search?"

Rule of thumb: if you need an answer today, AEOeye. If you're standing up a monitored, reported-on GEO function, AthenaHQ's setup is worth it.

sections.heading: Which one should you choose?
sections.body:
Choose **AEOeye** if you want to know — for free, today — whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini recommend your brand; if you're a solopreneur, small team, or marketer who wants a quick, honest competitive read without a contract or sales call; or if you simply want to scope the problem before spending. It's the low-risk way to find out whether AI visibility is even an issue for you.

Choose **AthenaHQ** if you're a mid-market or enterprise team, an agency managing multiple brands, or an e-commerce business with budget already allocated to AI search; if you need historical dashboards, sentiment trends, citation analytics, and ROI reporting to satisfy stakeholders; and if you're prepared for credit-based pricing and possibly an Enterprise tier for multi-region or API needs.

Many teams do both in sequence: run AEOeye first to confirm there's a gap worth closing and to see who's winning, then graduate to a paid platform like AthenaHQ once the program needs continuous monitoring. Starting free costs you nothing and makes the eventual buying decision sharper.

keyTakeaways: AEOeye is free and instant — you see whether AI engines recommend your brand before paying anything, with no contract or sales call.
AthenaHQ has no free tier or true free trial; the entry point is Self-Serve at $295/mo (discounted ~$95 first month, paid upfront).
AthenaHQ's credit model (3,600 credits, ~1 per AI response) can run out mid-month, with overages around $0.08/credit, making real cost hard to forecast.
Key AthenaHQ features — ACE citation engine, multi-region/persona, API, SSO — are Enterprise-only (custom, often $2,000+/mo); Self-Serve is single-country.
AthenaHQ is genuinely stronger for ongoing analytics: historical dashboards, sentiment trends, citation tracking, and ROI reporting for enterprise teams.
Best path for many: start free with AEOeye to scope the gap, then move to AthenaHQ when you need continuous, reported-on monitoring.

faqs.q: Does AthenaHQ have a free trial?
faqs.a: No. AthenaHQ has no free tier and no true free trial. The cheapest way in is the Self-Serve plan at $295/month, softened by a discounted first month (around $95) that still requires upfront payment. AEOeye, by contrast, lets you run a full multi-engine visibility audit for free before spending anything.

faqs.q: How much does AthenaHQ really cost per month?
faqs.a: The sticker price is $295/month for Self-Serve with 3,600 credits, where roughly one credit equals one tracked AI response. Teams monitoring many prompts across multiple engines or regions can exhaust those credits mid-month and buy overages (about $0.08/credit, or $100 per 1,250), so the actual bill often runs higher. Enterprise is custom, commonly starting around $2,000+/month.

faqs.q: Which AI engines does each tool cover?
faqs.a: AEOeye blind-queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini to show whether you're recommended and who outranks you. AthenaHQ also tracks the major engines (including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, and Grok) and adds deeper ongoing analytics like sentiment trends and citation tracking on its paid plans.

faqs.q: Is AEOeye a full replacement for AthenaHQ?
faqs.a: Not entirely, and we won't pretend otherwise. AEOeye is the best free, instant way to see your AI visibility and competitive position. AthenaHQ is stronger for sustained, enterprise-grade monitoring — historical dashboards, citation analytics, and ROI reporting. A common approach is to start with AEOeye to scope the problem, then adopt a paid platform when you need a continuous program.

Mid-market to enterprise teams, agencies managing multiple brands, and e-commerce businesses (Shopify/GA4) with budget allocated to prove AI-search ROI. If you're a solopreneur or small team who just wants a quick, honest look at your AI visibility, AEOeye's free instant audit is the more practical starting point.
